title: Swiss Military Launches Alpine Club to Tap India's ₹5,000-Crore Mass Premium Luggage Market
excerpt: The new sub-brand enters with 36 hard luggage options priced from ₹6,500 and targets tier 2 and tier 3 cities where demand for branded travel gear is rising fast.
body:
• Swiss Military has launched Alpine Club, a new sub-brand targeting India's mass premium travel gear segment estimated at ₹5,000 crore
  • The brand debuts with 36 hard luggage SKUs across three collections — Miles, Helix, and Vortex — priced between ₹6,500 and ₹7,500
  • Initial rollout focuses on Delhi NCR, Telangana, Gujarat, Bihar, and Jharkhand, with plans for exclusive brand outlets and expansion into soft luggage

Swiss Military has launched Alpine Club, a new sub-brand aimed squarely at the growing number of Indian travelers who want branded luggage without paying premium prices. The launch adds 36 hard luggage options to the market, starting at ₹6,500, and targets a segment the company estimates at ₹5,000 crore.

The move signals a broader shift in India's travel gear market. Luggage purchases, long concentrated among premium buyers in major cities, are expanding into smaller cities and towns as more Indians travel domestically and internationally.

Three Collections, Five Markets

Alpine Club's debut lineup spans three hard luggage collections: Miles, Helix, and Vortex. Prices range from ₹6,500 to ₹7,500, placing the brand below most premium luggage options while keeping it within the branded category.

"India's travel gear market is undergoing a decisive shift, with demand expanding well beyond the exclusive premium segment."

— Anuj Sawhney, Managing Director, Swiss Military

The company has identified Delhi NCR, Telangana, Gujarat, Bihar, and Jharkhand as its initial markets and has invested approximately ₹5 crore in the rollout. Plans include opening Exclusive Brand Outlets across these regions as Swiss Military works to build retail presence beyond metro areas.

Betting on Tier 2 and Tier 3 Cities

The strategy reflects a structural change in India's travel economy. Airport passenger traffic across smaller cities has grown steadily as low-cost carriers expand routes and middle-class incomes rise. For luggage brands, the opportunity lies in consumers who are upgrading from unbranded products but are not ready to pay ₹15,000 or more for established premium names.

Swiss Military is targeting a 3% to 5% share of the mass premium travel gear market within three years and expects Alpine Club to contribute nearly one-third of its overall revenue during that period. The company currently operates across 26 countries with over 300 products in its portfolio.

What Comes Next

The initial Alpine Club range is focused entirely on hard luggage. Soft luggage and additional travel gear categories are planned as part of a longer-term expansion. For Swiss Military, the sub-brand model allows it to compete in the mass premium segment without diluting its core positioning.

Digvijay Tiwari, Vice President of Marketing and Sales at Swiss Military, said the company will focus on retail visibility, wider distribution, and building consumer awareness for the new label. For Indian travelers watching their budgets, the ₹6,500 entry point puts branded hard luggage within reach for the first time.
